questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which focus is strongest for an informative speech?

feedback.text: This is too vague to guide a speech.

answer.text: B. Organized preparation helps speakers deliver clearer presentations.

feedback.text: Correct. This focus is specific and supports organized informative speaking.
This does not give a clear informative purpose.
This is broad and unfocused.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.02

Which set best develops an informative point?

feedback.text: This is incomplete because it lacks support and reasoning.
A topic alone is not developed.
This does not develop information.
Correct. This pattern explains information clearly.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Source: Rehearsing aloud helps speakers notice unclear parts before presenting. Which paraphrase is accurate?

answer.text: A. Practicing out loud can help speakers find confusing sections before the presentation.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps the source meaning in new words.

answer.text: B. Speakers should not revise unclear parts.

feedback.text: This contradicts the source.

answer.text: C. Rehearsing aloud makes every speech perfect.

feedback.text: This exaggerates the source meaning.
This adds an unrelated and inaccurate idea.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which speech product follows quality format expectations?

feedback.text: This is not a speech-ready format.

answer.text: B. A title with no main points.

feedback.text: This is incomplete because the speaker needs main points to organize the message.

answer.text: C. Introduction, focus, main points, support, transitions, and conclusion.

feedback.text: Correct. These parts create a complete speech format.
This does not support presentation quality.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.01

Which structure best explains a process?

feedback.text: Unrelated examples do not explain a process.
Random order makes the process hard to follow.
Correct. A process is clearest when steps are presented in order.
Hidden structure does not guide the audience.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.04

Which sentence follows standard English conventions?

answer.text: A. My speech explains how note cards support delivery.

feedback.text: Correct. This sentence uses standard capitalization, grammar, and wording.

answer.text: B. my speech explain note card ideas.

feedback.text: This has capitalization and agreement errors, so it is not ready for speech notes.
This has a subject-verb agreement error.
This needs capitalization.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.05

Which phrase uses precise academic speech vocabulary?

feedback.text: This is vague and informal.
This is not precise academic vocabulary.
This is informal and unclear.
Correct. This is precise vocabulary for speech organization.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which main point supports the focus "Planning helps speakers communicate clearly"?

feedback.text: This is unrelated to planning and clear communication.

answer.text: B. Outlining ideas helps the audience follow the speech order.

feedback.text: Correct. This point supports planning and clarity.
This is unrelated because it does not connect to planning or clear speech communication.
This does not support the focus.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.02

Which support best fits "Visual aids clarify information"?

answer.text: A. A chart can show a pattern that may be hard to explain with words alone.

feedback.text: Correct. This support explains how a visual aid clarifies.
This is too vague because it names the tool but does not explain how it helps the audience understand.
This does not explain clarity.
This is related but not enough support.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Which choice is closest to copying rather than paraphrasing?

answer.text: A. A new sentence that keeps the source meaning.

feedback.text: This describes a paraphrase.

answer.text: B. A short note in the speaker's own words.

feedback.text: This can be useful if accurate.

answer.text: C. The source sentence with only one word changed.

feedback.text: Correct. This is too close to copying.

answer.text: D. A restatement with a new sentence pattern.

feedback.text: This supports paraphrasing.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

What makes notes speech-ready?

answer.text: A. They force the speaker to read every word.

feedback.text: This weakens natural delivery.

answer.text: B. They give short cues for focus, points, support, and transitions.

feedback.text: Correct. Short cues support clear delivery.
Unrelated phrases do not guide speaking.
Speech notes should make points easy to find.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.01

The word "however" usually signals which relationship?

feedback.text: Sequence is signaled by words such as first or next.
Cause is signaled by words such as because.
However does not define a term.
Correct. However signals a different or opposing idea.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.02

Which sentence gives reasoning?

feedback.text: This does not explain anything about why timing helps the speaker or audience.

answer.text: B. A timer can measure a speech.

feedback.text: This is support, not reasoning, because it gives evidence without explaining why it matters.
This is a transition because it moves to another topic instead of explaining support.

answer.text: D. This matters because timing helps the audience follow without feeling rushed.

feedback.text: Correct. This explains why support matters.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which transition best connects organization to support?

feedback.text: This is vague because it does not show how the next idea connects to the previous idea.

answer.text: B. After organizing the points, the speaker should add support that explains each idea.

feedback.text: Correct. This transition shows a clear relationship.
This does not connect ideas.
This is too casual and unclear.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.04

Which revision corrects "my notes helps me present"?

feedback.text: This keeps the capitalization and agreement errors from the original sentence.
This fixes capitalization but not agreement.
Correct. This fixes capitalization and subject-verb agreement.
This still needs capitalization even though the agreement problem has been corrected.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.01

Which plan uses cause and effect?

answer.text: A. Rehearsal builds familiarity, so nervousness may decrease.

feedback.text: Correct. This shows a cause and result.

answer.text: B. Silent practice differs from peer practice.

feedback.text: This compares two options.

answer.text: C. Speech notes include focus and support.

feedback.text: This lists parts of a plan, but it does not show a cause and an effect.
This is chronological order.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which format part closes the speech?

feedback.text: A hidden topic weakens the speech.
A random detail does not close the speech.
Correct. The conclusion closes the speech and returns to the focus.
A support point develops the body, not the closing.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.02

Which support is too general?

answer.text: A. A timer can show whether the introduction takes too long.

feedback.text: This is specific because it gives a concrete rehearsal tool and purpose.

answer.text: B. A transition can show contrast between two ideas.

feedback.text: This is specific because it identifies a communication move and its function.

answer.text: C. A note card can list three main points.

feedback.text: This is specific because it names a tool and a clear planning detail.
Correct. This is too general and does not explain how practice helps.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Why should paraphrased source information keep the original meaning?

answer.text: A. So the speech communicates borrowed ideas accurately.

feedback.text: Correct. Accurate paraphrase protects the source meaning.

answer.text: B. So the speaker can avoid understanding the source.

feedback.text: Understanding is required.

answer.text: C. So the speaker can change facts freely.

feedback.text: Changing facts is inaccurate.

answer.text: D. So the speaker can remove the main idea.

feedback.text: Removing the main idea weakens accuracy.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which conclusion best fits a speech about preparation?

feedback.text: This is unrelated because it introduces a new topic instead of closing the preparation speech.

answer.text: B. Careful preparation helps speakers organize, support, and deliver clearer presentations.

feedback.text: Correct. This conclusion restates the focus and major points.
This does not restate the focus.
This is vague because it does not restate the focus or summarize the speech's key ideas.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.01

Which structure compares two practice methods?

feedback.text: This shows time order, but it does not compare two practice methods.
Correct. This structure explains similarities and differences.
This explains why a result happens.
This explains a term, but it does not show similarities and differences.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.05

Which word is most precise for a speech plan?

feedback.text: Correct. Transition is precise academic vocabulary for speech organization.
This is vague because it does not identify a clear speech-planning concept.
This is informal and does not use precise communication vocabulary for a speech plan.
This is too general because it does not name a specific speech part or communication action.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.02

Which answer best explains the role of support?

feedback.text: The focus is still needed.
Support should connect to the point.
Reasoning is still needed.

answer.text: D. Support gives details that help explain a point.

feedback.text: Correct. Support helps the audience understand the point.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which product is incomplete?

answer.text: A. Outline with focus, points, support, transitions, and conclusion.

feedback.text: This includes major parts.

answer.text: B. Notes with point and support cues.

feedback.text: These can support delivery.

answer.text: C. Title only with no speech sections.

feedback.text: Correct. A title alone is incomplete.

answer.text: D. Checklist with format and convention checks.

feedback.text: This supports quality work.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which question checks coherent focus?

answer.text: A. Does every main point support the same central idea?

feedback.text: Correct. This checks whether the speech stays focused.

answer.text: B. Is the speech as long as possible?

feedback.text: Length does not prove focus.
Unrelated points weaken focus.

answer.text: D. Did the speaker copy a source?

feedback.text: Copying does not check focus.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q26

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.02

Which transition signals sequence?

feedback.text: However signals contrast, so it does not show the order of steps in a sequence.
In contrast signals comparison, not sequence.
Because signals cause, so it does not show step-by-step order.

answer.text: D. First, choose the main point you need to support.

feedback.text: Correct. First signals sequence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q27

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Source: Note cards can help a speaker remember the order of ideas. Which paraphrase is accurate?

feedback.text: This changes the source meaning.

answer.text: B. Note cards can help speakers keep their ideas in order.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps the source meaning.
This contradicts the source.

answer.text: D. Order does not matter in speeches.

feedback.text: This contradicts the source.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q28

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.04

Which sentence is ready for speech notes?

answer.text: A. the outline show three planning points

feedback.text: This has capitalization and agreement errors, so it is not ready for speech notes.
This has an agreement error.
Correct. This sentence follows standard English conventions.

answer.text: D. the outline shows the three points.

feedback.text: This needs capitalization before it is ready for speech notes.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q29

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which checklist item supports speech format?

answer.text: A. The plan includes only random facts.

feedback.text: Random facts weaken format.
The focus should be clear because it guides the speaker and audience.

answer.text: C. The plan includes transitions between main points.

feedback.text: Correct. Transitions are part of quality speech format.
A conclusion is needed because it closes the speech and reinforces the message.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q30

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.01

The word "therefore" signals what relationship?

feedback.text: Contrast is signaled by however.
Correct. Therefore signals a result or conclusion.
Therefore does not define a word.
Therefore does not signal random order.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q31

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.02

Which support should be removed from a speech about note cards?

feedback.text: Correct. This is unrelated to note cards.

answer.text: B. Short notes can keep the speaker from reading a full script.

feedback.text: This supports the topic.

answer.text: C. A note card can list the three main points.

feedback.text: This supports the topic.

answer.text: D. Note cards can include transition cues.

feedback.text: This supports the topic.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q32

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which speech plan would be hardest for an audience to follow?

feedback.text: This can help an audience follow because ideas are presented in time order.
This helps listeners understand how one idea connects to the next.

answer.text: C. A plan with related main points.

feedback.text: This supports focus because the ideas connect to the same message.

answer.text: D. A plan with random order and unrelated points.

feedback.text: Correct. Random order and unrelated points weaken understanding.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q33

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.02

Which phrase best introduces reasoning?

feedback.text: This does not explain support.
This does not signal reasoning.
This signals a topic shift.
Correct. This phrase signals explanation of why support matters.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q34

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Which statement about paraphrase is true?

answer.text: A. It should change the source meaning.

feedback.text: This makes the paraphrase inaccurate.
Copying is not paraphrasing.

answer.text: C. It should restate the source accurately in new wording.

feedback.text: Correct. A paraphrase keeps meaning while changing wording.

answer.text: D. It should remove the important idea.

feedback.text: Removing the idea weakens accuracy.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q35

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which note is too vague?

feedback.text: Correct. This does not give a clear point or support.
This gives a specific cue.
This gives a clear cue because it names a point the speaker can follow.
This gives a relationship cue.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q36

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.01

Which feature signals an example?

feedback.text: However signals contrast.
Correct. This phrase signals that an example is coming.
Finally signals sequence or closing.
Because signals cause, so it does not introduce an example.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q37

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.05

Which phrase is most academically precise?

feedback.text: This is vague and informal.
Correct. This phrase precisely names a communication concept.
This is too general because it does not name a specific communication concept.
This is informal and unclear.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q38

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which choice best supports oral presentation?

answer.text: A. Notes that hide the main point.

feedback.text: This weakens delivery because the speaker may lose the central idea.
Random sentences do not guide delivery.

answer.text: C. A copied paragraph with no labels.

feedback.text: This may cause reading and confusion.

answer.text: D. Notes with short cues for each main point.

feedback.text: Correct. Short cues help the speaker present without reading a full script.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q39

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.02

Which support and reasoning pair is strongest?

answer.text: A. Support: practice is good. Reasoning: it is good.

feedback.text: This repeats without explanation.

answer.text: B. Support: notes exist. Reasoning: notes exist.

feedback.text: This repeats and is vague.

answer.text: C. Support: a timer shows section length. Reasoning: the speaker can revise parts that run long.

feedback.text: Correct. This gives specific support and explains why it matters.

answer.text: D. Support: speeches happen. Reasoning: they happen.

feedback.text: This does not develop a point.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_Assessment_Q40

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which statement best summarizes Unit 2 mastery?

answer.text: A. A strong informative speech plan has focus, organization, support, paraphrase accuracy, transitions, and quality format.

feedback.text: Correct. This summarizes Unit 2 mastery.

answer.text: B. Support and transitions are not important.

feedback.text: They are essential to clear informative speaking.

answer.text: C. Paraphrase means changing the source meaning.

feedback.text: Paraphrase must keep meaning accurate.

answer.text: D. A speech plan only needs a topic.

feedback.text: A topic alone is incomplete.
